title: Daily Life - Trying To Sleep
audio: mp3/236. Daily Life - Trying To Sleep.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we're talking a little bit about going to sleep or not being able to sleep.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们要谈一些关于睡觉或无法入睡的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We are having some sleeping problems and we're actually going to check out a couple of words related to this topic right now on Vocabulary Preview.
segments.zh: 我们有一些睡眠问题，我们现在实际上会在词汇预览中查看与该主题相关的几个单词。

segments.en: Vocabulary Preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预习。

segments.en: Okay, so the first word is actually the technical word that describes being unable to sleep.
segments.zh: 好的，所以第一个词实际上是描述无法入睡的技术词。

segments.en: It's called insomnia.
segments.zh: 它被称为失眠症。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So if you have insomnia, it means that you can't fall asleep.
segments.zh: 所以如果你有失眠症，这意味着你不能入睡。

segments.en: You can't sleep.
segments.zh: 你睡不着。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is a pretty serious condition.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个相当严重的情况。

segments.en: For example, if you have insomnia and you don't sleep for three or four nights, you're not going to do very well at work, right?
segments.zh: 例如，如果你有失眠症并且你三四个晚上都没有睡觉，你的工作就不会做得很好，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Or if you're studying, you're tired at school, you can't concentrate.
segments.zh: 或者，如果你在学习，你在学校很累，你无法集中注意力。

segments.en: So it's a very big problem.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常大的问题。

segments.en: What's that other word though?
segments.zh: 另一个词是什么？

segments.en: We have insomnia, but we also have another interesting disorder.
segments.zh: 我们有失眠症，但我们还有另一个有趣的疾病。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: If somebody is able to sleep but walks while they're sleeping, that person is called a sleepwalker.
segments.zh: 如果有人能够睡觉但在他们睡觉时走路，那个人被称为梦游者。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And you don't actually just have to walk to be a sleepwalker.
segments.zh: 而且您实际上不必步行即可成为一名梦游者。

segments.en: You can do any number of strange things like basically acting like you're awake when you're not.
segments.zh: 你可以做许多奇怪的事情，比如基本上你不醒着就表现得像醒着一样。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So some people get up and walk, actually go outside.
segments.zh: 所以有些人起身走路，实际上出门。

segments.en: Some people get dressed.
segments.zh: 有些人穿衣服。

segments.en: Some people go downstairs and cook.
segments.zh: 有些人下楼做饭。

segments.en: Yeah, that's right.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: And the worst is the people who eat because they gain weight and they don't know why.
segments.zh: 最糟糕的是那些吃东西的人，因为他们体重增加了，他们不知道为什么。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So sleepwalking is what you do.
segments.zh: 所以梦游就是你的工作。

segments.en: And if you do this, you're called a sleepwalker.
segments.zh: 如果你这样做，你就会被称为梦游者。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Sleepwalk is the verb.
segments.zh: 梦游是动词。

segments.en: Sleepwalker is the noun or the person.
segments.zh: 梦游者是名词或人。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we've taken a look at two words that we're going to find in our dialogue today.
segments.zh: 所以我们看了我们今天在对话中要找到的两个词。

segments.en: Why don't we go now and listen to the dialogue for the first time.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不现在就去听第一次对话。

segments.en: Alex, what's up with you?
segments.zh: 亚历克斯，你怎么了？

segments.en: You look dreadful.
segments.zh: 你脸色真差。

segments.en: Hey, Jill.
segments.zh: 嘿，吉尔。

segments.en: I don't know.
segments.zh: 我不知道。

segments.en: I've been having trouble sleeping these past few weeks.
segments.zh: 这几周我一直睡不好。

segments.en: I usually lie in bed for hours trying to get to sleep.
segments.zh: 我通常在床上躺几个小时试图入睡。

segments.en: I've tried stretching and different breathing techniques before going to bed.
segments.zh: 我在睡觉前尝试过拉伸和不同的呼吸技巧。

segments.en: I've tried eating and not eating different foods.
segments.zh: 各种食物我都试过吃，也试过不吃。

segments.en: I've even tried counting sheep.
segments.zh: 我什至试过数羊。

segments.en: And then when I finally get to sleep, I have these really disturbing nightmares.
segments.zh: 然后当我终于入睡时，我有这些非常令人不安的噩梦。

segments.en: So I usually wake up in a panic and more tired than before I went to sleep.
segments.zh: 所以我通常会在恐慌中醒来，比睡前更累。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: Maybe you should get that checked out.
segments.zh: 也许你应该检查一下。

segments.en: Maybe you're stressed.
segments.zh: 也许你压力太大了。

segments.en: Just take some sedatives.
segments.zh: 吃点镇静药吧。

segments.en: Works for me.
segments.zh: 我觉得行。

segments.en: Every so often having some melatonin on hand helps me when I have trouble sleeping.
segments.zh: 当我难以入睡时，每隔一段时间就会有一些褪黑激素帮助我。

segments.en: It works on all kinds of sleeping disorders.
segments.zh: 它适用于各种睡眠障碍。

segments.en: It's the stuff pilots use to regulate their sleeping patterns.
segments.zh: 这是飞行员用来调节他们的睡眠模式的东西。

segments.en: I heard of that.
segments.zh: 我听说过。

segments.en: But does that apply to Alex's situation?
segments.zh: 但这适用于亚历克斯的情况吗？

segments.en: Yeah, sure.
segments.zh: 好啊，当然。

segments.en: Why not?
segments.zh: 为什么不呢？

segments.en: Sounds like he only has transient insomnia since it's a recent thing so taking melatonin should do the trick.
segments.zh: 听起来他只有短暂的失眠，因为这是最近的事情，所以服用褪黑激素应该可以解决问题。

segments.en: But shouldn't he be looking into why it's been happening?
segments.zh: 但他不应该调查为什么会发生吗？

segments.en: Well, aren't you the little psychologist?
segments.zh: 哟，你还成了小心理学家了？

segments.en: Our buddy's having trouble sleeping.
segments.zh: 我们的朋友睡不着。

segments.en: It's easy and curable.
segments.zh: 这很容易治好。

segments.en: It's not something freakish like if he was a sleepwalker.
segments.zh: 又不是什么梦游之类的怪事。

segments.en: Well, there's that too.
segments.zh: 嗯，也有这个原因。

segments.en: Alright we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So obviously this person not only has insomnia but also has nightmares, sleepwalks, a mess.
segments.zh: 所以显然这个人不仅有失眠症，而且还有噩梦、梦游、乱七八糟的东西。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And you can tell when someone hasn't been sleeping well.
segments.zh: 你可以知道某人什么时候睡得不好。

segments.en: They have that look like there's bags under their eyes or they just look really tired.
segments.zh: 他们的眼睛下面有袋子，或者看起来很累。

segments.en: And so the friend here says, Alex, you look dreadful.
segments.zh: 所以这里的朋友说，亚历克斯，你看起来很可怕。

segments.en: That's right, dreadful.
segments.zh: 没错，可怕。

segments.en: So this is an adjective and it's a way to describe someone that looks terrible.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个形容词，它是一种描述看起来很糟糕的人的方式。

segments.en: You look horrible.
segments.zh: 你看起来很可怕。

segments.en: You look tired.
segments.zh: 你看起来很累。

segments.en: You look sleepy.
segments.zh: 你看起来很困。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this is not a compliment.
segments.zh: 所以这不是恭维。

segments.en: This is something that you say when you're worried about someone.
segments.zh: 这是您在担心某人时说的话。

segments.en: So for example, if someone's really, really tired, you say, you look dreadful.
segments.zh: 例如，如果某人真的非常累，你说，你看起来很可怕。

segments.en: Or if someone is wearing very dirty clothes, they don't look like they went home yesterday, you say, what's wrong?
segments.zh: 或者如果有人穿着很脏的衣服，他们看起来不像昨天回家了，你说，怎么了？

segments.en: You look dreadful.
segments.zh: 你脸色真差。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: I think you can also use it to describe objects or maybe food, right?
segments.zh: 我想你也可以用它来描述物体或食物，对吧？

segments.en: This lasagna is dreadful.
segments.zh: 这千层面太可怕了。

segments.en: It means it's very bad.
segments.zh: 这意味着它非常糟糕。

segments.en: And you don't want to say that to the person who cooked it, of course.
segments.zh: 当然，你不想对做饭的人这么说。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Alright, so the person obviously because is suffering from insomnia looks dreadful.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这个人显然是因为患有失眠症，看起来很可怕。

segments.en: And he was explaining what he does to try to fall asleep.
segments.zh: 他正在解释他做了什么来试图入睡。

segments.en: For example, counting sheep, stretching, and he also said that he tried different breathing techniques.
segments.zh: 例如，数羊、伸展，他还说他尝试了不同的呼吸技巧。

segments.en: Okay, so basically a technique is an approach to something, a kind of method.
segments.zh: 好的，所以基本上一种技术是对某事的一种方法，一种方法。

segments.en: But in this case, we're talking about breathing techniques.
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，我们谈论的是呼吸技术。

segments.en: So for some people, one breathing technique is breathing in through your nose and breathing out through your mouth.
segments.zh: 所以对于一些人来说，一种呼吸技术是通过你的鼻子呼吸，然后通过嘴巴呼吸。

segments.en: Like that.
segments.zh: 就这样。

segments.en: That's one kind of technique.
segments.zh: 这是一种技术。

segments.en: So a technique, as you say, is a way of doing something.
segments.zh: 因此，正如您所说，技术是一种做事的方式。

segments.en: So breathing techniques are different ways of breathing.
segments.zh: 所以呼吸技巧是不同的呼吸方式。

segments.en: So maybe you will relax, so maybe you'll fall asleep, things like this.
segments.zh: 所以也许你会放松，所以也许你会睡着，这样的事情。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: It's one of those things that you might learn about in a yoga class, for example.
segments.zh: 例如，这是您可能在瑜伽课上学到的东西之一。

segments.en: There's different breathing techniques.
segments.zh: 有不同的呼吸技巧。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And you can combine techniques with other words as well, adding the ing.
segments.zh: 您也可以将技术与其他单词结合起来，添加 ING。

segments.en: For example, you have walking techniques, maybe to put less stress on your knees.
segments.zh: 例如，你有步行技巧，也许是为了减少你的膝盖压力。

segments.en: Or running techniques, swimming techniques.
segments.zh: 或跑步技巧，游泳技巧。

segments.en: I think there's a technique for almost everything.
segments.zh: 我认为几乎所有东西都有一种技术。

segments.en: Just about anything you can do, there's a technique for it.
segments.zh: 几乎任何你能做的事情，都有一种技术。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Yeah, yeah, for sure.
segments.zh: 是的，是的，当然。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And well, moving on, he was talking about his nightmares and he described his nightmares as disturbing.
segments.zh: 好吧，继续前进，他在谈论他的噩梦，他形容他的噩梦令人不安。

segments.en: He has disturbing nightmares.
segments.zh: 他有令人不安的噩梦。

segments.en: Okay, well, I think this is an important word to cover here, Marco, because we've heard the verb to disturb before.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为这是一个重要的词，马可，因为我们以前听过动词打扰的动词。

segments.en: Like I'm sorry to disturb you.
segments.zh: 就像我很抱歉打扰你一样。

segments.en: It means I'm sorry to bother you.
segments.zh: 这意味着我很抱歉打扰你。

segments.en: But disturbing is an adjective.
segments.zh: 但令人不安的是形容词。

segments.en: It describes something that makes me very uncomfortable.
segments.zh: 它描述了一些让我非常不舒服的事情。

segments.en: Right?
segments.zh: 对吧？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So, for example, a lot of times in the news, we see very disturbing images, car accidents or fires or bombs.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，在新闻中很多时候，我们看到非常令人不安的图像、车祸或火灾或炸弹。

segments.en: And what's disturbing is when you see human beings who have been hurt.
segments.zh: 令人不安的是，当您看到受伤的人时。

segments.en: So images that make you really uncomfortable or sad, these are disturbing.
segments.zh: 所以让你真正不舒服或悲伤的图像，这些令人不安。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So disturbing nightmares are nightmares that are not very pleasant.
segments.zh: 所以令人不安的噩梦是不是很令人愉快的噩梦。

segments.en: They make him scared, maybe, or uncomfortable.
segments.zh: 他们让他害怕，也许，或不舒服。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Like a dream, for example, where your parents die.
segments.zh: 例如，你的父母死去的地方就像一个梦想。

segments.en: It's pretty disturbing.
segments.zh: 这很令人不安。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And well, one of his friends recommended, you know what?
segments.zh: 好吧，他的一位朋友推荐，你知道吗？

segments.en: Stop with all of this.
segments.zh: 停止这一切。

segments.en: Just take some sedatives.
segments.zh: 吃点镇静药吧。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So sedatives are a kind of medicine that help a person relax or that help make a person tired.
segments.zh: 所以镇静剂是一种帮助人放松或帮助一个人感到疲倦的药物。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So I think it comes from the verb to sedate.
segments.zh: 所以我认为它来自动词到镇静。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: And basically that is to calm down, to tranquilize.
segments.zh: 基本上就是冷静下来，平静下来。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So in this case, we're talking about a person, but you can also give an animal sedatives.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，我们谈论的是一个人，但你也可以给动物镇静剂。

segments.en: For example, if you want to take your dog on an airplane, the dog needs to relax.
segments.zh: 例如，如果你想带你的狗上飞机，狗需要放松。

segments.en: You give it some sedatives.
segments.zh: 你给它一些镇静剂。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And I think when he mentioned a specific name of a sedative, it's melatonin.
segments.zh: 我想当他提到镇静剂的具体名称时，它是褪黑激素。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So melatonin, melatonin is a chemical that our bodies naturally produce that help calm us down.
segments.zh: 所以褪黑激素，褪黑激素是我们的身体自然产生的一种化学物质，可以帮助我们平静下来。

segments.en: And so a lot of pharmaceutical companies or drug companies sell melatonin in a pill form.
segments.zh: 因此，许多制药公司或制药公司以药丸的形式出售褪黑激素。

segments.en: It's basically, it's a chemical that helps you relax.
segments.zh: 它基本上是一种化学物质，可以帮助您放松。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So obviously if you take melatonin, you're going to feel sleepy or you're going to be very relaxed and you're going to fall asleep a lot easier.
segments.zh: 所以很明显，如果你服用褪黑激素，你会感到困倦，或者你会非常放松，你会更容易入睡。

segments.en: Well, hopefully.
segments.zh: 好吧，希望。

segments.en: Hopefully.
segments.zh: 希望会吧。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, and well, the whole thing that we've been talking about, insomnia, sleepwalking, these are called sleeping disorders.
segments.zh: 所以，好吧，我们一直在谈论的整个事情，失眠，梦游，这些被称为睡眠障碍。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And remember, you might also hear the term sleep disorders.
segments.zh: 请记住，您可能还会听到睡眠障碍一词。

segments.en: They mean problems with sleeping.
segments.zh: 它们的意思是睡眠问题。

segments.en: So people who either cannot fall asleep or people who have bad dreams or people who sleep walk.
segments.zh: 所以要么睡不着的人，要么做坏梦的人或睡觉的人。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So a disorder is something of an illness or a condition that is not normal.
segments.zh: 所以疾病是一种疾病或不正常的疾病。

segments.en: So for example, as you said, a sleeping disorder or a sleep disorder, it means that you're not able to sleep properly or normally.
segments.zh: 例如，正如您所说，睡眠障碍或睡眠障碍，这意味着您无法正常或正常睡眠。

segments.en: But there are other kinds of disorders, right?
segments.zh: 但是还有其他类型的疾病，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And many people have heard of eating disorders.
segments.zh: 许多人听说过饮食失调。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's basically people who do not eat like everyone else.
segments.zh: 所以这基本上是不像其他人一样吃饭的人。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So that's what happens with a disorder.
segments.zh: 所以这就是疾病发生的事情。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we've taken a look at a lot of vocab.
segments.zh: 所以我们看了很多词汇。

segments.en: Now it's time for us to take a look at Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 现在是时候让我们看看 Fluency Builder 了。

segments.en: But before that, why don't we listen to the dialogue again?
segments.zh: 但在此之前，我们为什么不再听一次对话呢？

segments.en: Alex, what's up with you?
segments.zh: 亚历克斯，你怎么了？

segments.en: You look dreadful.
segments.zh: 你脸色真差。

segments.en: Hey, Jill.
segments.zh: 嘿，吉尔。

segments.en: I don't know.
segments.zh: 我不知道。

segments.en: I've been having trouble sleeping these past few weeks.
segments.zh: 这几周我一直睡不好。

segments.en: I usually lie in bed for hours trying to get to sleep.
segments.zh: 我通常在床上躺几个小时试图入睡。

segments.en: I've tried stretching and different breathing techniques before going to bed.
segments.zh: 我在睡觉前尝试过拉伸和不同的呼吸技巧。

segments.en: I've tried eating and not eating different foods.
segments.zh: 各种食物我都试过吃，也试过不吃。

segments.en: I've even tried counting sheep.
segments.zh: 我什至试过数羊。

segments.en: And then when I finally get to sleep, I have these really disturbing nightmares.
segments.zh: 然后当我终于入睡时，我有这些非常令人不安的噩梦。

segments.en: So I usually wake up in a panic and more tired than before I went to sleep.
segments.zh: 所以我通常会在恐慌中醒来，比睡前更累。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: Maybe you should get that checked out.
segments.zh: 也许你应该检查一下。

segments.en: So talking about dreaming, nightmares, insomnia, all of this, what do you do if you can't fall asleep?
segments.zh: 说到梦，噩梦，失眠，这一切，如果你睡不着，你会怎么做？

segments.en: I don't really have this problem personally because I could fall asleep anywhere, anytime.
segments.zh: 我个人并没有真正遇到这个问题，因为我可以随时随地睡着。

segments.en: I've heard some people take like warm milk before going to sleep.
segments.zh: 我听说有些人在睡觉前喝热牛奶。

segments.en: Some people take milk, although I also heard that dairy products before bedtime can make you have nightmares.
segments.zh: 有些人吃牛奶，虽然我也听说睡前乳制品会让你做噩梦。

segments.en: Oh, really?
segments.zh: 哦，真的吗？

segments.en: Like if you eat cheese before bed.
segments.zh: 就像你睡前吃奶酪一样。

segments.en: I've heard that as well.
segments.zh: 我也听说过。

segments.en: I've heard that if you have seafood before bed, you'll have nightmares as well.
segments.zh: 我听说如果你睡前有海鲜，你也会做噩梦。

segments.en: But actually, have you ever had a dream when you are doing something and you wake up in the middle of that?
segments.zh: 但实际上，当你做某事并且你在其中醒来时，你有没有做过梦？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: I remember once I was dreaming, I was drinking a soda and all of a sudden I woke up and I had my hand like in the air, like doing the action of me actually drinking the soda.
segments.zh: 我记得有一次我在做梦，我在喝汽水，突然醒来，我的手就像在空中一样，就像在做我真正喝苏打水的动作一样。

segments.en: Actually sometimes this happens to me when I'm falling asleep.
segments.zh: 实际上，有时当我睡着时，这会发生在我身上。

segments.en: I imagine I'm on a bike or something and I start to feel myself moving my legs and I wake up and I'm like, wait, wait, what am I doing?
segments.zh: 我想象我在骑自行车什么的，我开始感觉到自己在动我的腿，我醒来，我想，等等，等等，我在做什么？

segments.en: So the brain is very strange, I think, especially in those times when you're kind of asleep and you're kind of awake.
segments.zh: 所以我认为大脑很奇怪，尤其是在你睡着并且有点清醒的时候。

segments.en: Also when you wake up suddenly, I don't know if other people have experienced this, but you feel like you're falling or something, all of a sudden you just wake up with a shake.
